short: The Britons are the Celtic tribes that made up the main population of Britain from the 8th century BC to the 5th century AD. The Britons were not the original population of Britain; they settled the island in the early first millennium BC, coming from the continent and subduing much of the local Pictish population. The Britons bravely resisted the invasion of Britain by Roman legions, but by 84 AD the Romans had conquered most of the island. Freedom-loving and warlike, the Britons often rebelled against Roman authority. The Roman Empire held control of Britain until the early 5th century. During the Anglo-Saxon conquest of Britain (f5th and 6th centuries), most of the Britons were exterminated, some were driven into Wales, Scotland, Cornwall, and the Bretagne Peninsula.
history: A Germanic people consisting of several confederated tribes, it is thought that the Goths came from the Baltic coast region of northern Poland, possibly incorporating land as far afield as Sweden. They began to appear on the fringes of the Roman Empire during the 3rd century AD, their migration possibly forced by overpopulation and climate changes during the Dark Ages that made agriculture difficult in their homelands. Descending into the Balkan Peninsula via Dacia and Greece, they sacked several prominent cities in the region and probably destroyed the Temple of Artemis, one of the seven wonders of the ancient world. Gothic aggression was eventually checked by the Emperor Claudius II; a deal was struck which allowed them to remain settled on the borders of Rome's empire, in Dacia, in return for military assistance as auxiliaries and foederati. This state of affairs persisted for quite some time, with the Goths converting to Arian Christianity, and even becoming somewhat Romanised in the intervening years. However, around AD370, clashes with the Sarmatians, Alans and other steppe peoples, all under pressure from the newly-arrived, marauding Huns, turned the Goths into refugees, once again bringing them into conflict with the Roman Empire.
